mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a statistically significant positive correlation (p < 0.05) between the labor indicators and the return in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% suggests accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected future corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day (or 5-day) forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when the monthly CPIAUCSL acceleration persists.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in the ratio of orders to shipments (not directly observable here, but proxy via INDPRO trend) indicates supply-side stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines by > 3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive despite a statistically significant negative relationship (p < 0.05) between INDPRO decline and the return in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 3%, it indicates a shift toward monetary easing, which typically increases equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during the prior 60-day period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in job openings (not directly observable; use PAYEMS as proxy for labor activity) and a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a labor market tightness signal that is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases over the same period
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (p > 0.10) when the labor indicators move in the hypothesized direction.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent industrial production declines (INDPRO) and rising inflation (CPIAUCSL), investors anticipate future supply constraints, causing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days to turn negative.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is positive despite a significant negative cross-product (p < 0.05) between INDPRO and CPIAUCSL in the same window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the 2-year Treasury yield (not directly observable; use FEDFUNDS as proxy) below 1.5% over the next 60 days is interpreted as a risk-off environment that suppresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is not statistically lower than the prior 60-day average (p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS remains below 1.5%.
